- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.1) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) mid-horizon, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to counteract downward bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 1–2% upward bias for first 5 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.61, -0.22), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% to align with sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds model by >5% in 3+ consecutive days, apply “sentiment-driven correction” — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
